dos_1.resolved_part: Single-IP FD/memory exhaustion (~8192 connections from one IP) is closed; slot release on Close covers TLS/h1/h2/shutdown exits.
remaining: Global first-come cap without fairness or reservation: 8 IPv4 addresses x 32 (or one IPv6 /61 if IPv6 enabled; --listen :443 is dual-stack) hold all 256 slots indefinitely with one cheap request per connection every <90 s (IdleTimeout, server.go:353) or 5 s re-handshakes; reconnecting legitimate clients are refused service-wide.
Limits not operator-tunable (no flags in cmd/zeropw-linkd).
With --trust-proxy-header the connection limiter keys on the proxy address (connections.go:29-35): all clients share 32 connections.
No pre-TLS handshake rate limit per network; handshake CPU flood on 1/8 OCPU not measured.
dos_1.assessed_residual_severity: at least medium; release blocker for a public endpoint; original HIGH preserved
dos_1.resolution_condition: Fairness resistant to a small set of networks (reserve/evict favoring authenticated or established clients; short pre-first-request idle timeout), tunable limits, documented proxy behavior, measured load test on 1 GB / 1/8 OCPU.

new_findings.title: Session-challenge per-device quota exhaustible by anyone knowing an active device public key
new_findings.trigger_impact: From one or a few networks, keep 16 live purpose=session challenges per 60 s for a victim's public key; victim's challenge request gets 429 and its 1 h session cannot renew, losing device lists, TURN credentials, signaling and self-service revoke.
new_findings.existing_mitigations: Public keys are visible only to account members, former/revoked members and holders of old device lists; availability only; operator CLI unaffected; current members can already revoke.
new_findings.strongest_objection: Requires knowing the public key; reduces severity to LOW but does not refute.
new_findings.resolution_condition: Stateless HMAC challenges with bounded consumed-ID set, or per (device, requesting network) sub-quota.

new_findings.title: One account can hold all TURN allocations and bandwidth; docs imply per-device fairness
new_findings.trigger_impact: user-quota 24 x max 5 devices = total-quota 120 = bps-capacity/max-bps; one account (even honest fully meshed with restart overlap as sized by docs) exhausts TURN for all other accounts (486).
new_findings.existing_mitigations: Personal deployment usually single account; self-host §8 warns about other users.
new_findings.strongest_objection: Personal server target; accepted for severity, but self-host.md permits other users and cross-account TURN capacity is undocumented.
new_findings.resolution_condition: Document ~1 fully relayed account (~20 relayed pairs) capacity, or add per-account cap / lower user-quota.

new_findings.title: Service-CA trust check ignores macOS ACLs on CA file and ancestors
new_findings.trigger_impact: An ACE granting another user write/append/delete/add_file/delete_child/writesecurity on the CA or an ancestor passes the mode check; that user can replace roots used for service HTTPS and TURN TLS (next start); with network MITM, operator-level control of the victim's link account, no vault access.
new_findings.existing_mitigations: ACL must be set by owner/admin; MITM also needed.
new_findings.strongest_objection: User chose the CA location; reduces severity but contradicts code's own rationale.
new_findings.resolution_condition: On Darwin refuse CA paths with ACL entries granting modification to others, or document clearly that CA ACLs are unchecked.

new_findings.title: Healthcheck timer runs release probe binaries as unsandboxed root parsing coturn-controlled data
new_findings.trigger_impact: zeropw-turnprobe and zeropw-turnsweep run as root and parse STUN/TURN and coturn CLI responses (bespoke parsers in deploy/internal/turnclient, internal/coturncli) from the internet-facing turnserver process; a coturn compromise plus a parser logic bug crosses into root unnecessarily.
new_findings.existing_mitigations: Go memory safety; first-party artifacts; bounded parsers.
new_findings.strongest_objection: Exploitable Go parser bug unlikely; accepted, hence LOW.
new_findings.resolution_condition: Run probe/sweep as zeropw-linkd (runuser or User=) with zeropw-turnsweep.service-level hardening.

new_findings.title: State I/O re-resolves paths after directory checks; with attacker-writable parent on macOS the seed can be read via an fd opened before chmod -N
new_findings.trigger_impact: Attacker who can rename entries in the state dir's parent swaps in an own dir with an inheritable allow-read ACE after prepareStateDir; victim's temp device.json inherits it; attacker opens it during the multi-millisecond /bin/chmod exec window; chmod -N cannot revoke the open fd; seed written then read. Linux unaffected (zero group mask).
new_findings.strongest_objection: Exotic precondition; accepted, hence LOW, but breaks documented 'cleared before first byte' guarantee.
new_findings.resolution_condition: Do all state I/O relative to the pinned directory descriptor (os.Root/openat/renameat), or refuse a state directory whose parent is writable by others.

new_findings.title: 'Saturated month stays below 10 TB' is false for 31-day months and ignores overhead
new_findings.trigger_impact: 3,750,000 B/s x 2,678,400 s = 10.04e12 B in a 31-day month before IP/UDP/ChannelData, TCP/TLS framing, API and ACME egress; 'capped at 30 Mbit/s in total' hides per-direction semantics. Static arithmetic; coturn accounting not measured.
new_findings.existing_mitigations: Month-long saturation unlikely; budget alerts (docs correctly say they do not stop charges).
new_findings.strongest_objection: Margin, not design flaw; accepted, hence LOW.
new_findings.resolution_condition: Lower bps-capacity with headroom (e.g. <=3.5 MB/s) or state 30-day, payload-only, per-direction assumptions.

new_findings.title: Release/coturn-bundle digests are self-attesting; bundle extraction less strict than release extraction
new_findings.trigger_impact: Expected digest comes from a co-located .sha256; whoever substitutes the artifact substitutes the digest. Bundle tar as root without --no-same-permissions and without a listing check may install setuid bits or symlinks under /opt/coturn/<ver>. Nothing mechanically binds installed artifacts to a reviewed digest.
new_findings.strongest_objection: Operator is trusted; accepted for severity, but conflicts with 'only reviewed artifacts enter the protected release path'.
new_findings.resolution_condition: Out-of-band pinned reviewed digests (operator --sha256 from review record or signature); normalize bundle permissions and refuse non-regular entries as release.sh does.

new_findings.title: Docs and operations accuracy
new_findings.trigger_impact: (1) daemon.md §8.5 stale (omits chmod -N helper as macOS-specific code); §1 CA rule understates checks and does not state ACLs unchecked. (2) Lost-VM recovery does not warn that revocations after the last off-VM journal copy are lost and must be re-applied. (3) Admin-CIDR lockout guard only for IPv4 SSH_CONNECTION while ruleset permits SSH only for IPv4 admin CIDR.
new_findings.existing_mitigations: Existing session survives via established state; journal importance is mentioned generally.
new_findings.resolution_condition: Doc edits; IPv6-aware lockout guard or refusal.
